turns.speaker: Lena Varga
turns.text: New project, keeping records with you from the start. I'm a staff scientist in Wei Chen's lab. Plan: a genome-wide CRISPR knockout resistance screen in HAP1 cells against the compound AZ-5417, a quinone-containing investigational agent, followed by RNA-seq of the validated knockouts. Library is Brunello, 77,441 sgRNAs over 19,114 genes, lot L-88213. Target library coverage 500x at every step. Planned MOI 0.3, puromycin selection at 1.0 ug/mL starting 48 h post-transduction. Screen identifier SCR-01, transduction planned for 2026-01-14.

Logged: SCR-01, HAP1, Brunello lot L-88213, 500x coverage target, MOI 0.3, puromycin 1.0 ug/mL from 48 h, transduction 2026-01-14, compound AZ-5417. Two flags before you start. (1) 1.0 ug/mL puromycin is a plausible HAP1 number but it is passage- and serum-dependent; if you have not run a kill curve on this exact passage you are guessing. (2) At 500x coverage with 77,441 guides you need roughly 39 million selected cells per replicate, which drives your flask count more than anything else in the protocol - check that against your incubator space before the transduction, not after.

turns.speaker: Lena Varga
turns.text: Standing request on format. When you give me a protocol or a protocol change, give it as numbered steps, and put every concentration in bold and in ug/mL - not molar, not nM, not 'per flask'. I transcribe these onto the bench sheet and molar units are how we poisoned a whole plate last year.

Understood: numbered steps, concentrations bold and in ug/mL. Example in that format for the selection step as you have it now. 1. Seed HAP1 at 2.5e6 cells per T-175, 10 flasks per replicate. 2. Transduce with Brunello lot L-88213 at MOI 0.3 in the presence of polybrene **8 ug/mL**. 3. At 24 h, full medium change. 4. At 48 h, begin selection with puromycin **1.0 ug/mL**. 5. Maintain selection 7 days, feeding every 48 h, keeping **1.0 ug/mL** at each feed. 6. At day 7 harvest a 500x reference aliquot before splitting into compound and vehicle arms.

turns.speaker: Lena Varga
turns.text: SCR-01 is a failure and I want it on the record as such. Two problems. The functional titre was far below the p24 estimate: measured MOI came out at 0.12, not the 0.3 I planned, so my selected population is about 2.4 million cells per replicate instead of 39 million. That is 31x coverage, not 500x. Second, the puromycin at 1.0 ug/mL did not fully kill the untransduced control plate even at day 7 - about 15% survival. Calling SCR-01 dead rather than sequencing something I cannot interpret.

Agreed, do not sequence it - at 31x coverage the dropout distribution is noise and a negative result would be uninterpretable. Both failures have the same root cause worth noting: you took two numbers from elsewhere rather than measuring them on this passage. Recommendation for the repeat, in your format. 1. Titre the library by functional transduction on HAP1, not by p24, using a 6-point dilution and reading puromycin-resistant colonies at day 7. 2. Run a kill curve before anything else: 8 points of puromycin from **0 ug/mL** to **4.0 ug/mL** in 0.5 ug/mL steps, on the same passage you will screen, scored at 72 h and at day 7. Pick the lowest concentration giving 100% death of untransduced cells by day 7, not by 72 h. 3. Only then set the MOI.

turns.text: Kill curve goes up Thursday. Eight points, 0 to 4.0 ug/mL in 0.5 steps, as you said, same passage, scored at 72 h and day 7. Untransduced HAP1 only, three wells per point.

You need to know the concentration that kills all untransduced cells AND that your transduced cells tolerate for 7 days without visible stress - those are two different thresholds and the gap between them is your working window. Three wells per point is the minimum; if you have plate space use four, because at the low end you will be counting survivors by eye.

turns.text: Kill curve read. At 72 h everything above 1.0 ug/mL looks dead, but at day 7 there are survivors up to and including 1.0 ug/mL. If the repeat screen again shows any survival on the untransduced plate, go up rather than extending the selection, because extending selection costs you library representation.

turns.speaker: Lena Varga
turns.text: Mendes is asking which MAGeCK test to use as primary. He has 0.5.9.4 with both RRA and MLE available. Three replicates, paired vehicle and compound arms from the same transduction, plus a day-7 reference. What do you recommend as the primary analysis and what thresholds?

Recommendation: use MAGeCK MLE as the primary analysis with a paired design matrix, treating replicate as a covariate, and keep RRA only as a sanity check in the supplement. Thresholds: call a gene a hit at FDR < 0.1 with at least 3 of the 4 sgRNAs moving in the same direction. Reasons: your arms are paired by transduction, which MLE can use and RRA cannot; RRA's permutation null is poorly behaved when a handful of guides have very high counts, which happens in resistance screens because the resistant clones dominate; and the 3-of-4 guide requirement is what protects you from a single off-target guide carrying a gene. Do not lower FDR to 0.05 here - with three replicates you will lose real hits.

Re-make that library from retained RNA if you can - that is better than either option.
